findings.claim: The tests treat the chip as visible whenever aria-hidden is not "true", but aria-hidden is "false" in both the 'out' and 'back' phases. So nothing checks that the chip is still slid out at lapEnd + STILL_OUT, which is what AC4 asks for. If the chip slides back too early, every test still passes, even though in the browser it would be hidden behind BEST (and visibility:hidden under reduced motion).
findings.evidence: Mutation: race-ui.ts:22 `const NEW_BEST_BACK_TICKS = 0;` (or flip the comparison at line 83 to `since < NEW_BEST_BACK_TICKS ? 'back' : 'out'`). Trace for the first test in tests/ui/new-best-chip.test.ts:770: at lapEnd, since=0 gives phase 'back'. hud.ts:159 then sets aria-hidden="false", so `visibleNewBest`, which only checks `e.hidden || aria-hidden==='true'`, returns true. At lapEnd+STILL_OUT it is still 'back', so the test sees true. At lapEnd+GONE the phase is null and the test sees false. The test passes. In the real HUD, `.is-back` applies `transform: translateY(-100%)`, which puts the chip behind BEST (hud.css), and under reduced motion `.is-back { visibility: hidden }`. The player never sees NEW BEST. Grep for `is-out|is-back|ui-hud-new-best` in tests/ finds no matches.
findings.suggestedFix: In tests/ui/new-best-chip.test.ts (a new test, since tests are append-only), find the chip through the 'New best' label's parent and assert that it has class `is-out` at lapEnd and at lapEnd+STILL_OUT, and has neither `is-out` nor `is-back` at lapEnd+GONE. Alternatively, have hud.newBest set aria-hidden="true" in the 'back' phase too, so the existing visibility checks cover the slide-out window.

findings.claim: The class toggles are the only thing that makes the chip appear on screen: CSS keeps `.ui-hud-new-best` at visibility:hidden unless it has `.is-out`/`.is-back`. No test checks them. If they are removed, the NEW BEST chip never shows in the game, yet AC4, AC7 and AC8 all still pass because they only look at aria-hidden.
findings.evidence: Mutation: delete hud.ts:157-158 (`newBestChip.classList.toggle('is-out', …)` / `toggle('is-back', …)`). hud.ts:159 still flips aria-hidden to "false", so `visibleNewBest` (tests/game/best-lap-persistence.test.ts:497, tests/ui/new-best-chip.test.ts:748) and `visible` (tests/ui/new-best-stage.test.ts:842) still return true. In the browser, hud.css `.ui-hud-new-best { visibility: hidden; transform: translateY(-100%) }` never changes, so the chip stays invisible. Grep for `is-out|is-back` under tests/ finds 0 matches.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test that asserts the chip element has class `is-out` while NEW BEST should be visible. Better still, render the `new-best/hud` stage through harness/screens/browser.ts (`renderStage`) and assert that getComputedStyle(chip).visibility === 'visible' and that the chip's bounding box lies below `.ui-hud-best`.

findings.claim: The spec says 'A race UI with no track id saves nothing', but no test covers it. If the guard is weakened so the UI writes or reads under an undefined or empty id, the existing stages (which pass no trackId and default to localBestLaps) would read and write the real browser localStorage, and no test would fail.
findings.evidence: Mutation: race-ui.ts:257 `if (race.trackId !== undefined) {` becomes `{` with `bestLaps.write(race.trackId ?? '', ms)`. Grep for `trackId` in tests/ui finds only the two `game.startRace({ trackId: TRACK …})` calls in new-best-chip.test.ts. No test calls createRaceUi/reset without a trackId and then checks localStorage or the NEW BEST chip.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test that calls createRaceUi(root, {…}) and then ui.reset(...) without a trackId, syncs a view in which the player has finished a lap, and asserts that localStorage.length === 0 and that no NEW BEST chip is visible.

checked.how: Read every test and traced it against race-ui.ts. They use the literal key string. The parse mutations `ms > 0`→`>= 0` and dropping isFinite are caught by the '0' and 'abc' cases. AC2 checks that other tracks' keys are unchanged. AC3 checks NEW BEST visibility on every tick.

Both variants (getItem/setItem throwing, and the localStorage getter throwing) drive the race to the finish and assert the HUD best and the results time. The toHaveBeenCalled checks are in addition to those real assertions, not a replacement for them.

Timing comes from the tokens. Changing NEW_BEST_GONE_TICKS is caught, but changes to NEW_BEST_BACK_TICKS and to the out/back class are not (F1, F2). AC5 checks both labels and that the results show this race's best rather than the stored one.
It filters STAGES for a HUD-only stage with a visible 'new best' and a results stage with 'new best lap'. It depends on aria-hidden only (F2).

The AC4 test that compares against a stored best set between the two laps drives lap 2 tick by tick, so whether a lapEnd mutation is caught depends on the sign of l1<l2. I couldn't run it to find out, so I haven't reported it.
